children: GE Aerospace (GE) is buying CPP to boost capacity and speed airfoil tech. It expects ~$200M synergies by year three, aims for double‑digit ROIC post-close, and will expand production and delivery.
GE Aerospace backlog $210B, services backlog $170B. Strong engine induction demand. Company expects commercial services revenue to rise >20% in 2026, driven by maintenance demand.
GE Aerospace reported about 1,800 new engine orders at Farnborough, including IndiGo’s 1,000+ LEAP-1A engines and a 100-engine deal with Korean Air; orders include engines and services.
GE Aerospace (GE) expects LEAP engine shop visits to grow annually through 2030 and forecasts LEAP profitability to reach parity with the CFM56 by 2030; GE9X mid-seal certification is upcoming.
GE Aerospace to co-produce 99 F414-INS6 engines in India; technical issues cleared, HAL awaiting GE commercial proposal and India MoD AoN; contract possible this year or early next.
GE Aerospace CFO Rahul Ghai said the CPP deal isn’t a blueprint for broad vertical integration and GE won’t vertically integrate its entire supply chain amid ongoing constraints.
GE Aerospace (GE) reported a 50% YoY rise in GEnx engine deliveries in Q2 and expects stronger YoY and sequential delivery growth in Q3.
GE Aerospace shipped 10 F404-IN20 engines for Tejas Mk-1A; HAL plans to deliver 10 jets by March. GE committed to supply 12 more F404-IN20 engines by December.
